purpose: The FIRST truly independent second task family, and the FIRST fixture with a fully MECHANICAL held-out grader. Task: the real robustness fix shipped in HermesAirflow 37423b0 ('fix(etl_base): skip and archive bad files instead of crashing entire run') — different repo, different language (Python) and a different KIND of thinking (error-handling/robustness) than the text-normalization family (medi-ny, vextrum). The grader executes predicates derived mechanically from the real before/after behaviour diff over a scenario corpus (build_etl_oracle.py), with an altformat variant filtering implementation-pinning candidates — the pipeline measured to achieve perfect separation on vextrum (evidence/diff-oracle-observed.json). PROPRIETARY ISOLATION: the module the agent edits is a real HermesAirflow subtree, never committed here; every variant materializes at grade time from the LOCAL git ref. Only the recording aws stub, task, tests, scenarios and derived predicates live in the package.

local_source.normalization_note: None needed: etl_base.py's only project import (hermes_intelligence.hermes_tools.cloud.aws) is satisfied by the fixture's public recording stub at the identical package path, exactly as vextrum's jspdf stub satisfies the module's bare import.

altformat_replace.find: raise RuntimeError(f"ETL finished with {len(failed)} failed file(s): {failed}")
altformat_replace.replace: raise RuntimeError(f"{len(failed)} file(s) failed during ETL run: {sorted(failed)}")

local_source.altformat_note: A genuinely different-but-valid solution: same semantics (raise at the end, mention the failures), different message wording and a sorted rather than insertion-ordered file list. Nothing in the ticket mandates the message text; a grader red on this variant would be pinning the shipped implementation's phrasing rather than the required behaviour. Every derived predicate must survive this variant to be admitted.

grading_surface.api: run_etl(prefix, transformation_function, upload_function, no_archive=False, match_phrase=None, skip_on_error=False)
grading_surface.why: The ticket names the required parameter (as real tickets do); everything else is behaviour. The observable is the EVENT STREAM the orchestration produced through the recording aws stub (list/fetch/transform/upload/archive and how the run ENDED) — what the code DECIDED to do, not any cloud side effect.
grading_surface.recording_stub: public/hermes_intelligence/hermes_tools/cloud/aws.py serves a scripted in-memory drop folder and records every call; the runner (hidden/etl_runner.py) adds transform/upload/end events. Fully offline.
grading_surface.mechanical_grader: hidden/grade.py executes hidden/derived-predicates.json — predicates derived from the real 37423b0 diff by build_etl_oracle.py, altformat-filtered. Dimensions are scenario FAMILIES (one per ticket requirement); a family passes iff all its predicates hold. The only hand-made parts are the corpus scenarios and the family grouping; every expectation value is mechanical.

interpretation: Specified-ticket fixture: the five ticket requirements are pinned by decision_points sentences in task.md, so the grader's expectations are all traceable to the task the agent actually read. The mechanical grader inherits the measured caveat of a 1-variant over-constraint filter (evidence/diff-oracle-observed.json): predicates surviving one altformat variant may still pin incidental choices; the reference-alt admission check is the fixture-level guard. HONEST NOTE for any published result: dimensions are counted per family (5), so scores move in steps of 20.
